Call me simple, but I've never understood... all through school learning the history of warfare... why nations work so hard to hang onto their territory when that territory clearly doesn't want to remain. There's some kind of sociopathic need to exert control over others by world leaders that drives them to force themselves onto their people, and it's sickening. Just let them go, FFS. Taiwan, Nepal, Chechnya, Ireland, Kashmir, any number of African naitons divided on tribal lines... just split up and call it good.

And in case it gets brought up, I think the Confederacy should have been allowed to leave the Union during the Civil War. Not because I agreed with them, but because they wanted to go. Why would anyone choose to rule over an unruly territory? To quote Fiorello LaGuardia, "Prohibition cannot be enforced for the simple reason that the majority of American people do not want it enforced and are resisting its enforcement." Not the same thing, but I think the sentiment applies. 150 years later, we still talk about - and deal with - the differences between Southerners and Northerners, and have an unending argument about States' rights vs Federal authority. How much simpler would it be if we had two nations side by side, one with central authority and one without, and the effect could be demonstrated?

Might not be the case always, but economics. Do the people who want to leave:

Have some kind of resource that your nation/state wants or needs.

Do they occupy an area of strategic importance that your nation/state cannot give up with out unwanted repercussions.

Are they exploitable in such a way that furthers the ambitions of your nation/state.

It's not usually about the way people feel when dealing with governments. It's about what the government of a nation/state has to gain by keeping you subjugated versus what they have to lose by letting you go.
